title: Account Conservation Sprint Playbook — Renewal Risk Assessment & Exec Escalation Template
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a tactical, timeboxed sprint playbook for 'conserving' at-risk accounts ahead of renewal. Focus: move accounts from Risk T2/T3 into a stable renewal posture within a 4-week sprint window. Use for commercial and mid-market tiers; adapt cadence for enterprise (longer timeline + exec SKUs).

Audience and when to run this sprint:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM) flags an account with a risk score >= threshold (see scoring).
- Trigger when renewal date is within 90 days and engagement signals show decline or critical issues unresolved.
- Activate cross-functional squad when score indicates Tier 2 or Tier 3 risk.

Risk scoring quick matrix (use numeric score 0-100):
- Product usage decline (30): >30% drop in MAU/weekly active feature usage = 20–30 points depending on severity.
- Support severity (25): unresolved sev1/blocked tickets in last 30 days = 20–25 pts.
- Business health (20): contract value change/organizational changes = 10–20 pts.
- Financial signals (15): late invoices, procurement delays = 10–15 pts.
- Sentiment / exec engagement (10): negative NPS/comments, missed QBRs = 5–10 pts.
- Tier thresholds: 0–39 = T0 (healthy), 40–64 = T1 (monitor), 65–84 = T2 (intervene), 85–100 = T3 (urgent escalation).

Early-warning signals (automated & manual):
- 3-week drop in core endpoint calls or embeddings per seat.
- Fewer than 1 engineering syncs in 30 days for integration customers.
- Recent regressions reported on production evals or quality alerts.
- Contract owner change or procurement pause.

Conservation sprint roles and responsibilities:
- Sprint Lead: assigned CSM — coordinates the daily stand, single point of contact.
- Technical Lead: Solutions Engineer — triages infra/model issues, owns remediation work.
- Success Ops: prepares tracking sheet, metrics, and run-rate impact.
- Escalation Sponsor: VP Customer Success or GM — elevated when T3.
- Legal/Finance liaison: for contractual/Collections blockers.

4-week sprint template (week-by-week milestones):
Week 0 (pre-sprint, 3 business days)
- Collect baseline: usage dashboard snapshot, open tickets list, recent emails, contract peer.
- Quick-win log: list 2–3 low-effort actions (e.g., quota bump, temporary token increase, one-off training).
- Assign owners and schedule daily 15-min stand.

Week 1 (stabilize)
- Technical triage: Solutions Engineer reproduces issues, prioritizes fixes.
- Customer comms: CSM shares sprint charter, clear fast mitigations, expected outcomes.
- QBR prep: gather updated adoption metrics for an ad-hoc mini-QBR if requested.

Week 2 (remediate)
- Deploy fixes / run pilot changes: measure before-and-after on key metrics.
- Business alignment meeting with customer execs to reframe value props tied to usage.
- Escalate procurement blockers to Finance liaison.

Week 3 (accelerate adoption)
- Enablement: targeted training sessions for power users; produce tailored playbooks (runbooks).
- Incentives: offer limited-time credits or professional services hours for implementation.
- Re-measure risk score; if still T3, prepare exec escalation packet.

Week 4 (close and recommend)
- Present remediation results and proposed renewal terms.
- Close remaining tickets, document any outstanding commitments and timelines.
- Decision: move to renewal, extend sprint (if in-flight), or handover to churn remediation special ops.

Tactical mitigation plays (pick per-case):
- Fast technical patch + hotfix prioritization (pledged SLA for fix window).
- Data/quality rollback or model pin to previous stable checkpoint for regression cases.
- Dedicated mini-retainer of SE hours to ship integration improvements.
- Temporary rate/throughput adjustments to meet ramp expectations.
- Financial accommodations: short-term credits, deferred billing, or trimmed scope proposal.
- Exec sponsor intro + customer success plan signed by both parties.

Exec escalation packet (when moving to T3):
- One-page summary: current risk score, primary drivers, key customer stakeholders, last 30-day timeline, and proposed 30/60/90 day plan.
- Customer impact metric: concrete delta (revenue at risk, MAU decline %, feature deprecations).
- Ask: specific exec action required (e.g., VP intro, contract concession authority, PS allocation).
- Attachments: incident timeline, support ticket list, relevant GitHub/PRs or runbook links.

Sample escalation subject and opener (email):
Subject: "Escalation: [Account] — Renewal at risk (T3) — Action requested by [date]"
Opener: "Quick summary: [Account] currently scores {score} (T3). Core issue: [short statement]. Impact: [revenue at risk / x% usage drop]. Requested support: [1-2 asks]. We recommend a 30-minute sync w/you this week to align on next steps."

Tracking and metrics (use Success Ops sheet template):
- Sprint tracker columns: Account, Renewal date, Risk score baseline, Current score, Sprint start, Sprint end, Owner, Primary blocker, Action items (owner + due), Exec escalated (Y/N), Outcome.
- Success metrics to show at close: usage delta, tickets resolved (count & sev), time-to-fix, revenue preserved, NPS delta if available.

Communication templates (CSM -> customer):
- Sprint kickoff: clear charter, expected timeline, and commit list.
- Mid-sprint status: weekly note with progress against the 3 top blockers.
- Closure: summary of what changed, business outcome, and renewal recommendation.

Post-sprint playbook and retro:
- 48-hour retrospective with squad: what moved the needle, what blocked us, and recommendations for playbook updates.
- If renewal successful: create a 90-day value plan and schedule check-ins at weeks 2/6/12.
- If unsuccessful: capture churn root cause, update risk models, and ensure handoff notes for churn ops.

Checklist (quick reference):
- [ ] Baseline snapshot saved to account folder
- [ ] Daily 15-min stand scheduled and owner assigned
- [ ] Top 3 mitigation plays selected and owners assigned
- [ ] Exec escalation packet ready if score > 84
- [ ] Finance/legal items flagged and owner assigned
- [ ] Sprint tracker updated at least twice per week

Notes and playbook caveats:
- Adapt scope for enterprise accounts: longer runway, legal review, and PS-led remediation.
- Preserve audit trail: every commitment to customer must be logged in CRM and ticketing system.
- Maintain conservative financial concessions: prefer time-limited offers tied to adoption milestones.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Sprint tracker (copy): [linked_artifacts: JIRA: CS-4567]
- Exec packet template: Confluence/CS-RENEWAL-123
- Escalation Slack channel: #cs-escalations (use only after CSM/SE triage)

Owner notes: This doc is intentionally tactical and short-form so CSMs can spin up a 4-week conservation sprint quickly. Feedback welcome — add real examples to the appendix (anonymized) after each closed sprint so the playbook evolves.
